headline: AT&T and OpenAI are working together to build AI tools for AT&T's in-house legal department.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: announced on 8 Oct, before the window, and no terms, cost or timetable are given.
importance_line: What changed is that a large telecom company is building AI workflows with OpenAI for its legal work, which affects its in-house lawyers first, then outside law firms that handle its routine matters, and the doubt is that no terms or results are given and the cut in outside work is Artificial Lawyer's own guess.
summary: Artificial Lawyer reports, citing AT&T's announcement of 8 Oct 2026, that AT&T LegalEdge, the telecoms company's AI-first in-house legal group set up in January, is partnering with OpenAI to develop AI-enabled legal workflows across the AT&T legal department. AT&T says LegalEdge has handled nearly 100 matters in its first six months and its general counsel David McAtee says “legal judgment remains human”, while Artificial Lawyer's own reading is that the deal may mean lower legal spend and less routine work for outside law firms.
notes: Law360 (listed) is paywalled; text read in Artificial Lawyer, which relays AT&T's 8 Oct announcement (about.att.com/story/2026/att-legaledge.html returned 403).
